questions.q: Acute cholecystitis is most commonly caused by:
opts: Impaction of a gallstone in the cystic duct
Salmonella infection of the gall bladder
questions.why: About 90% of acute cholecystitis is calculous, due to a stone obstructing the cystic duct; acalculous disease occurs in the critically ill.

questions.q: Haemorrhages of bright red blood, burning pains, desire for cold drinks and fear in a tall, slender, sympathetic person suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Phosphorus: bright red bleeding, craves cold water.

questions.q: The normal platelet count in adults is about:
questions.why: Normal platelets are 150,000 to 450,000/uL; 4,000 to 11,000 is the WBC range and 4.5 to 5.5 million the RBC count.

questions.q: In 2020 the Revised National Tuberculosis Control Programme (RNTCP) was renamed the:
opts: National Programme for Control of Tuberculosis
questions.why: RNTCP became NTEP in 2020, reflecting the goal of eliminating TB.

questions.q: The medium routinely used to culture Mycobacterium tuberculosis is:
opts: Thiosulphate citrate bile salt sucrose agar
questions.why: Egg-based Lowenstein-Jensen medium is the standard solid medium for M. tuberculosis; colonies appear in 2 to 8 weeks.
